14618-robert-browning.title: Robert Browning
14618-robert-browning.creator: Unknown
14618-robert-browning.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Browning is confessedly a difficult poet, and his difficulty is by no means all of the kind which opposes unmistakable impediments to the reader's path. Some of it is of the more insidious kind, which may co-exist with a delightful persuasion that the way is absolutely clear, and Browning's "obscurity" an invention of the invertebrate.

arxiv-1612-06828.title: Semi-device-independent framework based on natural physical assumptions
arxiv-1612-06828.creator: Thomas Van Himbeeck, Erik Woodhead, Nicolas J. Cerf, Raúl García-Patrón, Stefano Pironio
arxiv-1612-06828.description: Abstract The semi-device-independent approach provides a framework for prepare-and-measure quantum protocols using devices whose behavior does not need to be characterized or trusted, except for a single assumption on the dimension of the Hilbert space characterizing the quantum carriers. Here, we propose instead to constrain the quantum carriers through a bound on the mean value of a well-chosen observable.

arxiv-2005-00375.title: Towards Visually Explaining Video Understanding Networks with Perturbation
arxiv-2005-00375.creator: Zhenqiang Li 1, 2], Weimin Wang 2, Zuoyue Li 3, Yifei Huang 1, and Yoichi Sato 1
arxiv-2005-00375.description: Abstract “Making black box models explainable” is a vital problem that accompanies the development of deep learning networks. For networks taking visual information as input, one basic but challenging explanation method is to identify and visualize the input pixels/regions that dominate the network’s prediction.

arxiv-2005-07161.title: A structure theorem for generalized-noncontextual ontological models
arxiv-2005-07161.creator: David Schmid, John H. Selby, Matthew F. Pusey, Robert W. Spekkens
arxiv-2005-07161.description: Abstract It is useful to have a criterion for when the predictions of an operational theory should be considered classically explainable. Here we take the criterion to be that the theory admits of a generalized-noncontextual ontological model. Existing works on generalized noncontextuality have focused on experimental scenarios having a simple structure: typically, prepare-measure scenarios.

arxiv-2302-12376.title: Multiverse Predictions for Habitability: Planetary Characteristics
arxiv-2302-12376.creator: McCullen Sandora *, Vladimir Airapetian, Luke Barnes, Geraint F. Lewis
arxiv-2302-12376.description: Abstract Recent detections of potentially habitable exoplanets around sunlike stars demand increased exploration of the physical conditions that can sustain life, by whatever methods available. Insight into these conditions can be gained by considering the multiverse hypothesis; in a multiverse setting, the probability of living in our universe depends on assumptions made about the factors affecting habitability.

arxiv-2310-05988.title: Dual Latent State Learning: Exploiting Regional Network Similarities for QoS Prediction
arxiv-2310-05988.creator: Ziliang Wang, Xiaohong Zhang, Kechi Zhang, Ze Shi Li, Meng Yan, Member, IEEE
arxiv-2310-05988.description: Abstract Individual objects (users or services) within a region usually have similar network states to each other because they usually come from the same region. Despite the similarity within regional networks, many existing techniques overlook this potential, thereby limiting the accuracy of Quality of Service (QoS) predictions.

arxiv-2402-08804.title: When Should you Offer an Upgrade: Online Upgrading Mechanisms for Resource Allocation
arxiv-2402-08804.creator: Patrick Jaillet, Chara Podimata, Andrew Vakhutinsky, Zijie Zhou
arxiv-2402-08804.description: Abstract In this work, we study an upgrading scheme for online resource allocation problems. We work in a sequential setting, where at each round a request for a resource arrives and the decision-maker has to decide whether to accept it (and thus, offer the resource) or reject it. The resources are ordered in terms of their value.

arxiv-2408-05377.title: More results on stack-sorting for set partitions
arxiv-2408-05377.creator: Samanyu Ganesh, Lanxuan Xia, Bole Ying
arxiv-2408-05377.description: Abstract . Let a sock be an element of an ordered finite alphabet A and a sequence of these elements be a sock sequence . In 2023, Xia introduced a deterministic version of Defant and Kravitz’s stack-sorting map by defining the ϕ σ \phi_{\sigma} and ϕ σ ¯ \phi_{\overline{\sigma}} pattern-avoidance stack-sorting maps for sock sequences.

arxiv-2409-01097.title: Nested Bregman Iterations for Decomposition Problems
arxiv-2409-01097.creator: T. Wolf, D. Driggs, K. Papafitsoros, E. Resmerita, C.-B. Schönlieb
arxiv-2409-01097.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by T. Wolf, D. Driggs, K. Papafitsoros, E. Resmerita, C.-B. Schönlieb. We consider the task of image reconstruction while simultaneously decomposing the reconstructed image into components with different features. A commonly used tool for this is a variational approach with an infimal convolution of appropriate functions as a regularizer.

arxiv-2507-17541.title: Approximating temporal modularity on graphs of small underlying treewidth
arxiv-2507-17541.creator: Vilhelm Agdur, Jessica Enright, Laura Larios-Jones, Kitty Meeks, Fiona Skerman, Ella Yates
arxiv-2507-17541.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Vilhelm Agdur, Jessica Enright, Laura Larios-Jones, Kitty Meeks, Fiona Skerman, Ella Yates. Modularity is a very widely used measure of the level of clustering or community structure in networks. Here we consider a recent generalisation of the definition of modularity to temporal graphs, whose edge-sets change over discrete timesteps; such graphs offer a more realistic model of many real-world networks in which connections between entities (for example, between individuals in a social network) evolve over time.

pmc-11677010.creator: Roberta Budriesi, Ivan Corazza, Simone Roncioni, Roberta Scanferlato, Dalila De Luca, Carla Marzetti, Roberto Gotti, Nicola Rizzardi, Christian Bergamini, Matteo Micucci, Davide Roncarati, Laura Beatrice Mattioli, Maria Digiacomo

Background: Three herbal extracts (Asparagus racemosus Willd., Tabebuia avellanedae Lorentz, and Glycyrrhiza glabra L.) were mixed with three essential oils (Foeniculum vulgare Mill., Mentha piperita L., and Pimpinella anisum L.) to formulate a product (HEMEO) whose active compounds include saponins and steroids in Asparagus racemosus, known for their anti-inflammatory properties; glycyrrhizin and flavonoids in Glycyrrhiza glabra, which exhibit gastroprotective and antispasmodic effects; menthol in Mentha piperita, contributing with antispasmodic and antimicrobial properties; and anethole and polyphenols in Pimpinella anisum, which modulate intestinal

pmc-11690088.title: DYING WITH DEMENTIA: CAREGIVERS’ OBSERVATIONS OF PHYSICAL AND/OR BEHAVIORAL/PSYCHOLOGICAL DECLINE IN OLDER ADULTS
pmc-11690088.creator: Cynthia Hovland, Christopher Mallett
pmc-11690088.description: Family caregivers of older persons with dementia have significant challenges across many domains. These reported problems encountered over their caregiving time are for many reasons, but what makes the caretaking difficult is complicated by both the unknown nature of the dementia disease and the dying trajectory.

pmc-12566443.title: Molecular Subtypes and Survival Patterns in Female Breast Cancer: Insights from a 12-Year Cohort
pmc-12566443.creator: Ionut Marcel Cobec, Ingolf Juhasz-Böss, Peter Seropian, Sarah Huwer, Vlad Bogdan Varzaru, Andreas Rempen, Aurica Elisabeta Moatar
pmc-12566443.description: Background and Objectives: Breast cancer is one of the most common cancers in women and the most common cause of cancer death. Hormone receptors, specifically the estrogen receptor (ER) and progesterone receptor (PR), as well as human epidermal growth factor receptor-2 (Her2), are tumor-specific markers used to guide breast cancer therapy.

pmc-13350614.title: Interleukin-8 in health and disease
pmc-13350614.creator: Chiara Bazzichetto, Emanuela Dell’Aquila, Margherita Veroli, Lorenzo Belluomini, Adele Bonato, Giovanni Bernardini, Michele Bevilacqua, Filippo Cattazzo, Andrea Dalbeni, Tarcisio Michele Tampu, Valentina Salari, Paolo Francesco Fabene, Claudio Luchini, Michele Milella, Fabiana Conciatori
pmc-13350614.description: Cytokines are among the main factors involved in indirect cell-to-cell communication in physiological and pathological conditions. In this way, cytokines are soluble and tissue-resident easily detectable biomarkers for the diagnosis and the prediction of clinical outcome, as well as drug targets.

pmc-13371813.title: Periodontitis and Stroke Onset, Medical Costs and Length of Hospital Stay: A 5‐Year Cohort Study
pmc-13371813.creator: Mizuki Saito, Yoshihiro Shimazaki, Toshiya Nonoyama, Yoshinori Inamoto
pmc-13371813.description: AimsTo evaluate the longitudinal association between periodontitis and stroke onset using medical claims data and also to assess the relationship between periodontitis and stroke‐related medical costs and length of hospital stay.Materials and MethodsIn total, 1997 individuals aged 75 or 80 years were included.

pmc-13449459.title: Genome-wide identification of NRAMP gene family in Brassica U’s triangle species and its response to Cadmium stress in B. napus
pmc-13449459.creator: Jie Liu, Furong Zhang, Xin Li, Haijuan Tang, Youran Deng, Kamran Ghaffor, Yuan Kong, Shixing Guo
pmc-13449459.description: BackgroundSoil cadmium contamination is a persistent environmental and agricultural problem worldwide, largely because it stays in the soil and can easily enter the food chain. In plants, the Natural Resistance-Associated Macrophage Protein (NRAMP) gene family plays key role in cadmium uptake, transport, and homeostasis.

pmc-13577620.title: Consumer Preferences for AI-Based Smart Home Medical Emergency Detection Among German Adults: Choice-Based Conjoint Analysis
pmc-13577620.creator: Inga Jagemann, Justin Baudisch, Thorsten Jungeblut, Günter W Maier, Gerrit Hirschfeld, Ivan Steenstra
pmc-13577620.description: BackgroundSmart home technology powered by AI can detect anomalies and make emergency calls, enabling residents to live safely and independently. However, the adoption of such technologies for medical emergency detection remains limited.ObjectiveThis study aimed to explore consumer preferences for AI-based smart home technology for medical emergency detection and identify predictors such as sociodemographic variables, AI literacy, and technology affinity.

pmc-13599963.title: Association between delayed transcatheter aortic valve replacement beyond 6 months and clinical outcomes in severe aortic stenosis: a retrospective observational study
pmc-13599963.creator: Ayumi Omuro, Shinichi Okuda, Yosuke Miyazaki, Masaki Tamitani, Junya Nawata, Yusuke Nakashima, Miho Fujita, Kaori Murakawa, Masamune Uchida, Yuki Furushimo, Hiroshi Kurazumi, Ryo Suzuki, Akihito Mikamo, Takayuki Okamura, Kimikazu Hamano, Motoaki Sano
pmc-13599963.description: ObjectiveEarly intervention for asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis (AS) has shown prognostic benefits; however, some patients undergo transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) after extended observation owing to mild symptoms or comorbidities. Although guidelines recommend surveillance of 6–12 months, the clinical implications of waiting beyond 6 months remain unclear.
